landscape.tagline: Three cheap reads before one expensive one.
landscape.narration: book-index.md picks one book to load per task, and today it only owns one size: the full one. Upstream already publishes two smaller ones. This design wires them in.

problem_solution.problem: book-index.md's escalation jumps straight from a cheap corpus heuristic to a 300-1000 line full book. Upstream ciembor/agent-rules-books now ships nano and mini tiers for the same 14 books, and none of them are vendored or used here.
problem_solution.solution: Vendor nano.md and mini.md alongside each book's existing full.md. Require a minimum of three nano loads before any book may be judgment-escalated to mini or full, and make full-tier loading conditional instead of automatic.
problem_solution.narration: The fix is not a bigger corpus. It is using the sizes that already exist instead of reaching for the biggest one every time.

beats.text: Grounding found the escalation policy itself violates its own stated cap, and a documented sync script that was never actually written.

Six divergent frames produced a ledger, a cold-storage index, a subagent-fan-out pattern, a live-fetch approach that a security classifier blocked outright, a pre-concatenated ladder file, and a panic-grep pre-filter.

The critic scored the ladder file highest, then flagged that its own stop-early discipline has no mechanical enforcement — the same failure mode this repo's Gate 4b history already lived through. The engineer chose to accept that same risk in a simpler, separate-files form instead of adopting the ladder file's mechanism.
3 nanos minimum, judgment-gated escalation to mini or full, separate files per tier, the old 1+1 cap rewritten to say so explicitly.

Answering a follow-up question about Review mode's mandatory 14-file security corpus load surfaced the same shape of problem — 2179 lines read unconditionally, every run, larger than a single full book. The fix folded into this design instead of spawning a new one: read each file's first ~30 lines (metadata plus summary, already structurally separate from its examples) unconditionally, then read the remainder in full unless the summary clearly rules out applicability — defaulting to full, not to skipping, on ambiguity. The opposite bias from book escalation, deliberately, because a missed security finding costs more than a wasted read.

alternatives.option: 3 nanos, then always the full book, unconditionally
alternatives.rejected_because: Defeats the point of a cheap tier, and breaks the existing cap with no replacement stated.
Solves auditability, a problem nobody named, at the cost of a new file surface.
Sized for 140+ books; this repo has 14.

alternatives.option: Live-fetch from upstream URLs at task time
alternatives.rejected_because: Blocked by a security classifier — a real injection and supply-chain risk.

alternatives.option: Pre-concatenated ladder file with a stop-early marker
alternatives.rejected_because: Scored highest, but its stop-early rule has no mechanical consumer.
Would need to ship as an agent, which ADR-0015 forbids.
The critic's starred survivor, deferred rather than bundled into this design.

alternatives.option: Judgment-gate the security corpus the same symmetric way as books (skip-on-ambiguity)
alternatives.rejected_because: A missed finding in a compliance-weighted report costs more than a wasted read; security stays biased toward reading in full.

architecture.narration: book-index.md becomes the single owner of a three-tier vendored shelf, with an explicit, stated ceiling on how much of it any one task may read. The security corpus gets the same shape of gate without a new file format.

beats.text: references/books/<name>/{nano,mini,full}.md — 42 files, replacing the current 14 full-only files.
book-index.md: load a minimum of 3 nano excerpts; escalate any one book to mini or full only when its principles are judged to matter; full is never automatic.
Design mode Stage 1 (Ground) and Stage 3 (Explore), and Review/Maintenance's corpus-to-book escalation, both read the new rule instead of the old 1+1 cap.

SKILL.md's Review mode security step: read the first ~30 lines of all 14 security corpus files unconditionally; read a file's remainder in full unless its summary clearly rules out applicability; ambiguity defaults to full, not to skipping.
